Adding technical detail for Alex and HealthMatrix:
- Replica placement: for Private deployments we follow the customer-specified region pins; there is no automatic cross-region replica for the pilot unless the customer requests disaster-recovery replication. For EU-only, we will not instantiate nodes outside eu-west-1 (we note region by cloud provider tag in our deploy tool).
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS via BYOK with separate CMKs per tenant. The CMKs remain under the customer's KMS account; Redwood's control plane requests decryption under a constrained IAM role scoped to the EU KMS key.
- Telemetry & logs: operator audit logs (who did what in the cluster) are retained by Redwood for 90 days by default and can be forwarded to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket in-region upon request. Application-level request logs (token-level telemetry) can be configured to never leave the customer VPC; default hosted control-plane metrics do include aggregated non-identifying telemetry but not full request bodies.
- Network egress: management/control-plane traffic for job orchestration may call back to our (regional) control plane endpoint; for Private with VPC peering this endpoint will be an EU-hosted endpoint and we do not traverse the US backbone for those calls. We will provide a network flow diagram and a short egress manifest (attached: kms-separation-notes-20260604.txt).

I've attached the redacted operator roster and a short technical note describing KMS scoping. If HealthMatrix needs a signed attestation that no standby exists outside EU we can produce a one-paragraph letter — legal will do the sign-off.

Irene Choi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
